title: A locally quasi-finite morphism with quasi-compact source has universally bounded fibres (Stacks 03JA)
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and assume $X$ is quasi-compact. Then the fibres of $f$ are universally bounded: there is an integer $n\geq0$ such that for every $y\in Y$ the fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field]) is a finite scheme over $\kappa(y)$, i.e. $X_y=\operatorname{Spec}B_y$ with $B_y$ a finite $\kappa(y)$-algebra, of degree $\dim_{\kappa(y)}B_y=\dim_{\kappa(y)}\Gamma(X_y,\mathcal O_{X_y})\leq n$; that is, $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ and the fibres of $f$ are universally bounded [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Definition Tag 03J4 and Lemma Tag 03JA.)

proof.text: *Finite affine covering.* Since $X$ is quasi-compact, there are finitely many affine opens $U_1,\dots,U_m\subseteq X$ ($m\ge0$) covering $X$ and affine opens $V_1,\dots,V_m\subseteq Y$ with $f(U_i)\subseteq V_i$: for each $x\in X$ choose an affine open $V_x\ni f(x)$ of $Y$ and an affine open $U_x\ni x$ of $X$ contained in the open $f^{-1}(V_x)$ (affine opens form a basis of the topology of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]); the $U_x$ cover $X$, and quasi-compactness gives finitely many of them covering $X$. (The affine opens form a basis: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis].)

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, first paragraph, lines 15505-15518

proof.text: *The pieces are quasi-finite.* Let $f_i=f|_{U_i}:U_i\to V_i$ be the restriction ($\iota_{V_i}\circ f_i=f\circ\iota_{U_i}$ for the inclusions of the open subschemes). By the local nature of local quasi-finiteness [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens] (Stacks 01TH (4)), $f_i$ is locally quasi-finite. As a morphism between affine schemes, $f_i$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], hence quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3). A locally quasi-finite quasi-compact morphism is quasi-finite [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] (Stacks 01TJ). So each $f_i$ is a quasi-finite morphism of affine schemes.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, first paragraph, lines 15505-15518 (with Lemmas Tag 01TH (4) and 01TJ)

proof.text: *Finite morphisms of affine schemes.* Let $\pi:Z\to V$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] with $Z$ and $V$ affine. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$; then $\pi=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ for a unique ring map $\varphi:A\to B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and since $\pi^{-1}(V)=Z$ the definition of a finite morphism says that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, say by $x_1,\dots,x_n$, so $A^{\oplus n}\to B$, $(a_1,\dots,a_n)\mapsto\sum a_ix_i$, is a surjective $A$-module map. Let $v\in V$ correspond to the prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ up to the isomorphism $\kappa(v)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification], so the fibre $Z_v=Z\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], with ring of global sections $C=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Tensoring the surjection with $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (right exactness of $-\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$) gives a surjective $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-linear map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)^{\oplus n}\to C$, so $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}C\le n$. The morphism $Z_v=\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a morphism of affine schemes, hence affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and the only nonempty open of the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the whole space, with preimage $\operatorname{Spec}C$, over which the ring map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to C$ is finite; so $Z_v$ is finite over $\kappa(v)$ of degree $\le n$. Hence $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $\pi$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound].

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, third paragraph, lines 15537-15552

proof.text: *Quasi-finite morphisms of affine schemes.* Let $g:U\to V$ be a quasi-finite morphism of affine schemes. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-affine-open-in-finite] (Stacks 03GU) there are an affine scheme $Z$, an open immersion $j:U\to Z$ and a finite morphism $\pi:Z\to V$ with $g=\pi\circ j$. The open immersion $j$ is an immersion (the identity of $U$, a closed immersion, followed by $j$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]), so $1$ bounds the degrees of its fibres [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-fibre-degree-one] (Stacks 03J9). By step 3 some integer $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $\pi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-composition-fibre-degree-bound] (Stacks 03J6) the integer $1\cdot n=n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $g=\pi\circ j$. Applied to the morphisms $f_i$ of step 2, this gives integers $n_i\ge0$ such that $n_i$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f_i:U_i\to V_i$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound].

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, second paragraph, lines 15521-15535 (Lemmas Tag 03GU, 03J9, 03J6)

proof.text: *The fibre of $f$ is covered by the fibres of the pieces.* Let $y\in Y$, let $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ with projections $p:X_y\to X$ and $q:X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and let $c:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y$ be the canonical morphism. For each $i$ the open subscheme $p^{-1}(U_i)$ of $X_y$, with the restrictions of $p$ and $q$, is a fibre product $U_i\times_XX_y$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]; pasting it with the cartesian square defining $X_y$ [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] shows that $p^{-1}(U_i)$ is a fibre product $U_i\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ of $f\circ\iota_{U_i}=\iota_{V_i}\circ f_i$ and $c$. The sets $p^{-1}(U_i)$ cover $X_y$ since the $U_i$ cover $X$. If $y\notin V_i$, then $p^{-1}(U_i)=\emptyset$, because $p$ maps $X_y$ into $f^{-1}(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and $f(U_i)\subseteq V_i$. If $y\in V_i$, the residue field of the open subscheme $V_i$ at $y$ is $\kappa(y)$ and the canonical morphism $c_{V_i}:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to V_i$ satisfies $\iota_{V_i}\circ c_{V_i}=c$ [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality]; the preimage of $V_i$ under $c$ is all of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, so $(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y),c_{V_i},\mathrm{id})$ is a fibre product $V_i\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], and pasting [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the square defining the fibre $(U_i)_y=U_i\times_{V_i}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ of $f_i$ with this square shows that $(U_i)_y$ is also a fibre product $U_i\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$. By uniqueness of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], $p^{-1}(U_i)\cong(U_i)_y$ as schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$. Thus $X_y=\bigcup_{i:\,y\in V_i}p^{-1}(U_i)$ is a covering by finitely many open subschemes, each isomorphic over $\kappa(y)$ to the fibre of $f_i$ at $y$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, first paragraph, lines 15505-15518 ('For $y \in Y$ it is clear that $X_y = \bigcup_{y \in V_i} (U_i)_y$ is an open covering')

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Put $N=n_1+\dots+n_m$. Let $y\in Y$. By step 5, $X_y$ is covered by the open subschemes $p^{-1}(U_i)$, $y\in V_i$, and by step 4 each of them is finite over $\kappa(y)$ with $\dim_{\kappa(y)}\Gamma(p^{-1}(U_i),\mathcal O)\le n_i$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-open-cover-degree-sum], $X_y$ is finite over $\kappa(y)$, i.e. $X_y=\operatorname{Spec}B_y$ with $B_y=\Gamma(X_y,\mathcal O_{X_y})$ a finite $\kappa(y)$-algebra, and $\dim_{\kappa(y)}B_y\le\sum_{i:\,y\in V_i}n_i\le N$. So $N$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$, which is the statement. (The fibre is affine with $\Gamma$ a finite-dimensional $\kappa(y)$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim].)
